app.about.intro: WOBD reads your car's check engine light codes and live data through a USB OBD-II adapter and explains them in plain English: how urgent each code is, what usually causes it, and what to tell your mechanic. There's nothing to install and it's free. Not sure what a code means? Try Code Search or the how-to guide.
app.about.needsAnswer: A car with OBD-II (US model year 1996 or newer), a USB ELM327-compatible adapter, and a laptop or Chromebook running Chrome, Edge, or Opera.
app.about.needsTitle: What do I need to use WOBD?
app.about.offlineAnswer: Yes. Code Search explains trouble codes offline, with no adapter or car needed.
app.about.offlineTitle: Can I look up a code without an adapter?
app.about.phoneAnswer: No. WOBD uses Web Serial, which phones and tablets don't support. Use a laptop or Chromebook.
app.about.phoneTitle: Does WOBD work on a phone?
app.about.privacyAnswer: Yes. Scan data stays in your browser. Only a search you choose to open, or a VIN lookup you agree to, leaves the site.
app.about.title: Free OBD-II scanner in your browser
app.about.whatAnswer: WOBD is a free OBD-II scanner that runs in your browser. It gives general information, not a professional diagnosis, so always confirm a problem before replacing parts.

replay.detectors.commLossExplanation: No gauge reported anything from {from} to {to} ({seconds} s). That can mean the ignition was turned off, the adapter lost its link, or the car stopped answering. A gap alone doesn't say which, and it is not a stall.
replay.detectors.loopChangeExplanation: Changed from "{previous}" to "{status}". Open loop is normal while the engine warms up and when coasting or under heavy load; closed loop is normal at steady cruise.
replay.detectors.loopFaultExplanation: The fuel system status read "{status}" for {seconds} s. The car's own status is worth checking with a code scan.
replay.detectors.loopFaultTitle: Fuel system reported a fault state
replay.detectors.loopFlappingExplanation: The fuel system changed between open and closed loop {count} or more times within a minute. Mixed driving (coasting, then accelerating) can do this. If it happens at a steady speed, it's worth a closer look.
replay.detectors.rpmExplanation: RPM moved between about {low} and {high} while the reported speed stayed near {speedRange}. This may be a gear shift or torque-converter change, a change in road load, or abnormal engine behavior. Review the data around {time} before drawing a conclusion.
replay.detectors.rpmTitle: RPM changed a lot at a steady speed
replay.detectors.stallExplanation: RPM dropped from about {rpm} to 0 and stayed there for {seconds} s while other gauges kept answering{movingText}. That fits an engine that stopped with the ignition on, but a deliberate shut-off, a start-stop system, or a bad RPM reading can look the same.
replay.detectors.stallMoving: , with the car still reading {speed} (some hybrids and start-stop cars do this normally)
replay.events.noneFound: Nothing unusual found. That is not a clean bill of health: WOBD only checks a few patterns.

replay.load.notWobdCsv: This doesn't look like a WOBD recording. Pick a CSV saved from WOBD's Live data recording.
replay.load.partialRecording: This recording was interrupted before it was saved, so it may end early.
replay.load.unknownPids: Skipped readings WOBD doesn't have a gauge for: {pids}. Any raw bytes saved in the file are kept, so a future WOBD can decode them.
replay.notes.confirmDifferentRecording: These notes were made for a different recording{name}, so their times may not line up with this one. Add them anyway?
replay.notes.errorCustomLabel: Give a custom note a short label.
replay.notes.errorFileUnreadable: That notes file is too big or unreadable.
replay.notes.errorNotNotesFile: That isn't a WOBD notes file.
replay.notes.errorTime: A note needs a time in the recording.
replay.notes.errorTooMany: That notes file has too many notes.
replay.notes.maximum: This recording already has {count} notes, the most WOBD keeps.
replay.notes.savedLocal: Saved in this browser only. Export them to keep a copy or share.
replay.notes.saveFailed: Couldn't save in this browser (storage is blocked or full). Export your notes to keep them.
replay.quality.assumedLocal: The timestamps have no time zone, so they are shown as local time as recorded.
replay.quality.clockJumps: where the clock jumped or drifted from elapsed time (possible clock change)
replay.quality.duplicateRows: repeated at the same moment (all kept)
replay.quality.elapsedOnly: No usable timestamps: only elapsed time is shown, and no date or clock time is guessed.
replay.quality.everyRow: Every row had a readable timestamp, in order.
replay.quality.malformedTimestamps: with a timestamp that couldn't be read (their elapsed time is still used)
replay.quality.missingTimestamps: with no timestamp (their elapsed time is still used)
replay.quality.outOfOrderRows: out of time order (played back in time order)
replay.quality.summaryClean: Recording quality · no timestamp problems found
replay.report.allPatternsListed: Every pattern WOBD found is listed, including routine ones and ones marked as false alarms.
replay.report.averageMethod: Samples are readings received, not separate events. The average is of readings, so gauges WOBD asked for more often count for more.
replay.report.detailLimit: Detail sections are shown for the first {shown} of {total} patterns. The rest are in the table above; use Replay to inspect them.
replay.report.disclaimer: This report is not a professional diagnosis. It lists what WOBD read from the car and a few patterns that may deserve a second look. Always confirm a problem before replacing parts.
replay.report.footer: WOBD session report{vehicle} · General information, not a professional diagnosis.
replay.report.gapCount_one: {formattedCount} gap, {gapTime} with no readings; {connectedTime} with readings
replay.report.gapCount_other: {formattedCount} gaps, {gapTime} with no readings; {connectedTime} with readings
replay.report.gaps: Gaps with no readings at all
replay.report.graphExplanation: Lines break wherever a gauge had no readings, and grey bands mark stretches when nothing answered at all. Orange bands are detected patterns; dashed red lines are your notes. Circles mark the highest and lowest points.
replay.report.methodDetectors: Pattern rules (detector set v{version}): a reading older than {fresh} s is ignored when compared; RPM swing of {rpmSwing} rpm within {rpmWindow} s at a steady speed above {speedMin} {speedUnit}; a new fuel-loop state must hold {loopDwell} s; a stall needs RPM above {stallRpm} just before dropping to 0 for {stallHold} s while other gauges still answer.
replay.report.methodExclusions: Diagnostic trouble codes, freeze-frame data and GPS location are not part of a recording, so they are not in this report.
replay.report.methodGap: A connection gap is a stretch longer than {seconds} s with no reading from any gauge. A gap alone never counts as a stall or a fault.
replay.report.methodGraphs: The recording was not changed. Graphs are simplified to fit the page but keep each highest and lowest point.
replay.report.methodSampling: Readings are taken one after another, not at the same instant, so two gauges at the same time are close but not simultaneous.
replay.report.notesLeftOut_one: {formattedCount} note was left out of this report.
replay.report.notesLeftOut_other: {formattedCount} notes were left out of this report.
replay.report.quietGauges: Some gauges stopped answering for a while while others kept going, so their graph lines break: {labels}.
replay.report.statesNotSummarized: Not summarized because they are states, not numbers: {labels}.
replay.report.subtitle: Diagnostic session report
replay.report.timestampProblems: Timestamp problems in the file (rows were kept unchanged): {problems}.
replay.report.vehicleNotEntered: Not entered (WOBD recordings do not store the vehicle)
replay.timeline.gap_one: No readings arrived during this stretch: {ranges}. The graphs show them as shaded bands. A gap doesn't say why (engine off, ignition off, or the adapter dropped out).
replay.timeline.gap_other: No readings arrived during these stretches: {ranges}. The graphs show them as shaded bands. A gap doesn't say why (engine off, ignition off, or the adapter dropped out).
replay.wobd.checksumMismatch: {name} does not match its checksum, so the file is damaged.
replay.wobd.confirmExcludeSource: Leave the original CSV out? The .wobd file will still keep every reading, but it won't contain your original file. WOBD only allows this when it can rebuild the CSV exactly.
replay.wobd.csvMissingColumns: That doesn't look like a WOBD recording (no {columns} column).
replay.wobd.csvMissingRecord: A record is missing, so the CSV cannot be rebuilt.
replay.wobd.damagedReadingsBlock: A block of readings is damaged.
replay.wobd.entryTooLarge: An entry ({name}) is too large to store.
replay.wobd.manifestMismatch: The manifest does not match the files inside.
replay.wobd.missingManifest: That file is incomplete (it has no manifest).
replay.wobd.missingReadings: Some readings are missing between blocks.
replay.wobd.newerVersion: That file was made by a newer WOBD. Update WOBD to open it.
replay.wobd.notesTooLarge: The notes in this file are too large.
replay.wobd.notRecordingFile: That is not a WOBD recording file.
replay.wobd.parameterListInvalid: The parameter list in this file is not valid.
replay.wobd.readingInvalid: A reading in this file is not valid.
replay.wobd.recordingDetailsInvalid: The recording details in this file are not valid.
replay.wobd.rowsDuplicate: {count} rows repeat an earlier reading. They are kept.
replay.wobd.rowsExact: {count} rows rebuild exactly as they were.
replay.wobd.rowsMalformed: {count} rows could not be read as readings (blank, malformed, or missing values). They are kept exactly as written and are not shown in graphs.
replay.wobd.rowsNormalized: {count} rows were readable, but their original text differs from how WOBD writes it (for example 0500 for 500). The original text is kept alongside.
replay.wobd.rowsOutOfOrder: {count} rows are out of time order. They stay in their original order.
replay.wobd.rowsRead: {count} data rows read; {readings} stored as readings.
replay.wobd.saved: Saved {name} ({size} KB). Your CSV was not changed.
replay.wobd.savedCsvRecordInvalid: A saved CSV record is not valid.
replay.wobd.sourceExcludedExact: The original CSV file is not stored. WOBD checked that the CSV can be rebuilt byte for byte from what is stored.
replay.wobd.sourceIncluded: The original CSV file is stored inside the .wobd file, byte for byte.
replay.wobd.sourceRequired: This file can't be rebuilt exactly without the original, so the original CSV was kept inside.
replay.wobd.unknownParameters: Parameters WOBD does not decode are kept: {pids}.
replay.wobd.unlistedEntry: The file has an entry the manifest does not list.
replay.zip.archiveTooLarge: The archive is larger than WOBD allows.
replay.zip.browserCannotDecompress: This file is compressed and your browser cannot open it. Please update your browser.
replay.zip.checksumFailed: An entry failed its checksum ({name}). The file is damaged.
replay.zip.damagedWobd: That is not a .wobd file, or it is damaged.
replay.zip.duplicateEntry: The archive lists the same entry twice.
replay.zip.encryptedOrStreamed: Encrypted or streamed entries are not supported.
replay.zip.entryTooLarge: An entry is larger than WOBD allows.
replay.zip.entryTooLargeForHeader: An entry is larger than it says it is.
replay.zip.extraData: The file has extra data after the archive.
replay.zip.fileTooLarge: That file is bigger than WOBD can open.
replay.zip.headerMismatch: An entry header does not match the archive directory.
replay.zip.highCompressionRatio: {name} is unusually compressible. That is normal for a car idling, but the file was not made by WOBD if it is not.
replay.zip.notReadable: Not a file I can read.
replay.zip.tooManyEntries: That archive has too many entries.
replay.zip.unknownEntry: The archive has an entry WOBD does not recognise ({name}).
replay.zip.unpackFailed: An entry is damaged and could not be unpacked.
replay.zip.unreadableName: An entry has an unreadable name.
replay.zip.unsupportedCompression: An entry uses a compression method WOBD does not support.
